transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO, Citrine Labs), Liam Chen (Eng Manager), Ava Gomez (SRE)

Summary (auto): Discussed p95 latency targets, concurrency needs, tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Samir our SE, um quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya: Hi Priya here, CTO at Citrine Labs.
[00:07] Liam: Liam, eng manager.
[00:09] Ava: Ava, SRE.
[00:12] Jordan: Great, the plan today is to understand your latency and throughput goals for the clinical assistant project and map Redwood's Hosted/Dedicated/Private options. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:22] Priya: Yeah we want to get pretty specific — our goal is real-time suggestions inside clinician workflow, so p95 matters more than avg. We're targeting p95 ~200 milliseconds for short prompts (<=64 tokens) and under 1s for longer streaming responses (~512 tokens).
[00:36] Samir: 200ms p95 is pretty ambitious, especially at 64 tokens. Are those end-to-end targets including network and client side, or just inference?
[00:44] Priya: End-to-end as measured from the UI. We know there's some wiggle room but we need to design against it.
[00:49] Samir: Understood. A few clarifying q's — what's your expected concurrency and qps?
[00:55] Liam: For phase one, 200 concurrent clinician sessions active, sustained during clinic hours, with spikes to 500 for peak. Average requests per second probably 60-100, but concurrency matters more.
[01:09] Jordan: Is streaming required, or could you tolerate non-streaming responses?
[01:12] Priya: Streaming is important for perceived latency for long responses. If the model can stream tokens progressively, clinicians feel it's faster.
[01:20] Ava: Also we have security constraints — data residency and private certs, and we need KMS integration for any PHI-like metadata.
[01:28] Jordan: Got it — so security + latency + concurrency. On the hosting side, we usually show three options: Hosted API (fastest to go live), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictability), and Private (VPC/on-prem for strict compliance). Tradeoffs are cost vs control vs setup time.
[01:45] Priya: Can you give rough latency numbers on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[01:49] Samir: Roughly, with our Hosted API using optimized kernels and prefix caching, for a 64-token request we can get 50-120ms median and p95 in the 150-300ms range depending on region and model choice; that's end-to-end in our measurements excluding customer network variability. For Dedicated, with pinned capacity and tighter colocation, p95 can drop by ~20-30% and jitter reduces. Private VPC/on-prem has similar latencies to Dedicated if you provision comparable GPUs, but there's an ops overhead.
[02:12] Liam: So Hosted might meet 200ms p95 in best case, but Dedicated gives more headroom. What's the tokens/sec throughput per GPU for the model sizes we're thinking about?
[02:22] Samir: For a 7B-ish dense model on an A100 80GB with quantization, you can see sustained 6k-12k tokens/sec depending on batch strategy; a 13B/70B family will be lower per-GPU. But real-world throughput depends on batching, KV cache reuse, and typical sequence lengths.
[02:39] Priya: We're evaluating a 13B open model tuned for medical prompts. We expect average output lengths ~200 tokens per response.
[02:48] Samir: Okay so at 200 tokens per response and 100 qps that's 20k tokens/sec total — so you'd want 2-3 GPUs for basic throughput with headroom, but concurrency/latency SLOs push you to more reserved capacity or better batching.
[03:02] Ava: We care about p95 under load — like if 200 conc sessions each generate a 200-token response concurrently, can you maintain p95 below 1s?
[03:13] Samir: Yes with Dedicated and autoscaling configured for that concurrency we can aim for p95 sub-1s for 200-token streams, but you'll want to pin model replicas and use continuous batching with size caps to avoid queuing spikes.
[03:26] Jordan: Quick note on streaming: our streaming path flushes tokens as they are generated and you can set chunk sizes. That reduces perceived latency but total end-to-end might still be similar; however p95 of first-byte is often much lower.
[03:39] Priya: That helps. For SLA purposes we measure both first-byte p95 and final-response p95. Target first-byte p95 <200ms, final-response p95 <1s.
[03:49] Samir: We can instrument both — Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns and first-byte traces per request, so you can create alerts on regressions.
[03:58] Liam: What's the typical cold-start effect? If model isn't warm, do you see big spikes in latency?
[04:03] Samir: Cold start can add 200-800ms depending on model and where weights are cached. In Hosted we keep popular models warm, but in Private you can control warm pools. For critical paths we recommend pinning at least one warm replica per region.
[04:17] Ava: For compliance, can Hosted support KMS and audit logs?
[04:21] Jordan: Hosted supports SOC2 and audit logs; for KMS-backed encryption of keys you might need Dedicated or Private depending on your KMS (we integrate with customer KMS in Private deployments, Dedicated has options for bring-your-own-key in some plans). We'll share the SOC2 and VPC docs.
[04:36] Priya: Great. On benchmarking — do you provide a runbook to replicate tokens/sec and p95 tests?
[04:41] Samir: Yes we have a benchmark spreadsheet and a script. It measures median/p95 first-byte and full-response latency across sequence lengths, and tokens/sec under synthetic and replay workloads. We'll send the template.
[04:52] Priya: We'd like to run that against Hosted first as a proof, then if needed bring Dedicated. How long does it take to onboard to Hosted for initial tests?
[04:59] Jordan: You can be running simple tests within hours; for production-like benchmark with region selection and streaming configs maybe a day. Dedicated provisioning is longer — a few days to weeks depending on capacity and contract. Private VPC/on-prem is the longest.
[05:13] Liam: Pricing for Dedicated — ballpark for an 8 GPU pool?
[05:17] Jordan: I'll send a draft estimate. It depends on GPU type and committed term — we'll include options in the doc.
[05:23] Ava: For our SRE team, we also need request tracing and the ability to reroute to fallback models on overload. Does Redwood support that?
[05:31] Samir: Yes automatic fallback policies and smart routing by latency/cost/region are supported. You can configure canary rollouts and A/B testing too.
[05:40] Priya: In the benchmark, can we see the difference between quantized and fp16 runtimes for our chosen model?
[05:46] Samir: Absolutely — the template includes toggles for quantization profiles and we can run side-by-side. Quantized runs reduce memory/cost and often improve throughput but may slightly impact output quality; we'll flag quality regression metrics.
[05:57] Priya: We need to be careful on hallucination/regression post-quantization.
[06:02] Samir: Agreed — Redwood Optimize recommendations include quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval prompts. We can attach your clinical prompt set to the eval to catch regressions.
[06:12] Liam: For concurrency handling, what's your recommended autoscaling policy?
[06:16] Samir: For latency SLOs you want predictive scaling with buffer headroom — e.g., scale when queue depth reaches X or predicted qps exceeds baseline by 20%. Also set burst capacity for short spikes. We'll provide a sample policy.
[06:29] Ava: For network topology, if we do Private VPC, will traffic between our app and Redwood Private plane remain within our VPC?
[06:36] Jordan: Yes Private deployments give you control of networking. The control plane can be customer-managed and we can integrate with your VPC; on-prem is fully air-gapped if needed.
[06:46] Priya: For our timeline — we'd like a pilot in next 6 weeks and a production rollout in 3 months if benchmarks look good.
[06:53] Jordan: That sounds reasonable. Pilot path: Hosted test -> Dedicated pilot (if needed) -> Private for full compliance.
[06:59] Liam: Can you run a quick example calculation for required GPUs? If we need 200 concurrent sessions each producing 200 tokens with streaming, what capacity do we need?
[07:10] Samir: Rough calc: 200 sessions * 200 tokens = 40k tokens in-flight. If your model generates at, say, 200 tokens/sec aggregate per GPU (depends on model and batch), you'd need ~200 GPUs — but that's naive. With batching and streaming, more realistic numbers: a well-tuned 13B on A100 might do 1k-2k tokens/sec per GPU with effective batching; then you'd need ~20-40 GPUs. But since many clinicians will be waiting for first bytes rather than full stream, you can optimize for first-byte latency by smaller batch sizes. We'll get you a concrete estimate after we run the replay benchmark with your traces.
[07:41] Priya: That's a big swing — makes sense. We'll share traces.
[07:45] Ava: We'll need an NDA in place before sharing PHI-adjacent traces, can you confirm?
[07:50] Jordan: Yes, NDA first. We'll send your legal contact our standard NDA.
[07:55] Priya: Good. Also curious about monitoring retention — how long are logs and token traces stored?
[07:59] Samir: Hosted comes with default retention (30 days) but enterprise options include longer retention or log export; Dedicated/Private gives more control. We'll include retention options.
[08:10] Liam: Any known pitfalls when moving from Hosted benchmark to Dedicated production?
[08:15] Samir: Often differences come from network colocation, warm pool sizing, and autoscaling tuning. Also model variants and kernel choices may differ slightly; we'll run model parity checks as part of the pilot.
[08:25] Jordan: Ok let's recap action items and next steps.
[08:28] Priya: Recap please.
[08:30] Jordan: Jordan to send benchmark spreadsheet + runbook + SOC2 and VPC docs; Samir to draft recommended Dedicated config and autoscaling policy; Citrine to share traces and target prompt set after NDA. We'll schedule technical deep dive with SREs next Tue 02/09.
[08:47] Priya: That works.
[08:49] Ava: I'll coordinate internally and send traces once NDA's signed.
[08:52] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:55] Liam: Thanks all.
